title: Di Resta wins the first DTM night race at Misano
dek: Paul di Resta won Race 1 at Misano from pole, 1.973 seconds ahead of Robin Frijns, who passed Edoardo Mortara on the last lap, while title rival Gary Paffett retired after contact with Mortara.

chapters.title: A new circuit, floodlights and a title fight
text: The DTM went to Misano on 25–26 August for the seventh round of the 2018 season, and it was a weekend of firsts. The series had never raced at the circuit near Rimini, and it had never raced in the dark. Qualifying was scheduled for 20:00 under floodlights and each race for a 22:30 start. Mobile lighting had been added at the pit exit and in several corners on top of the permanent floodlights, and the cockpits were lit so that the drivers could read their instruments. For most of the grid the track was unfamiliar, apart from those who knew it from GT racing.

At the top of the championship it was a Mercedes-AMG affair. Gary Paffett led the standings on 177 points, 29 ahead of his Mercedes team-mate Paul di Resta, who had won twice that year, at the Hungaroring and in Race 2 at Brands Hatch. Both had come out of Brands Hatch a fortnight earlier with their rivalry intact, and a pair of races on an unknown track, in the dark and possibly in the wet, offered the chance for the gap to swing either way.

The other talking point was in the BMW garage. Alex Zanardi, 51, was making a one-off guest appearance in a converted M4 DTM operated entirely by hand controls, the first time he had raced without his artificial legs. His own target was modest: he hoped to leave at least one other car behind him. Rain over the circuit on Saturday evening meant that the first night race would be run on a track that was wet, drying and changing all at once, and that tyre choice would matter as much as outright speed.

chapters.title: Di Resta takes pole in the rain
text: Qualifying was held in the wet, and the times fell steadily throughout. Most drivers stayed out for the whole session rather than make their usual two runs. René Rast, in the Rosberg Audi, led for much of it, setting the early benchmark of 1m50.579s and going fastest again with six minutes left. Di Resta then went quicker and Rast’s next improvement fell just short.

Mortara then moved right up to di Resta’s time, but the Scot improved again and again, finding more than half a second in the closing minutes, and he took pole with 1m46.826s. Mortara’s Silberpfeil Mercedes #48 was second, 0.469s back, which made the front row all-Mercedes. Rast, the reigning champion, was third at 0.575s, and Paffett, with a last-lap effort, was fourth, 0.608s off the pole time.

Timo Glock was the leading BMW in fifth in the RMR car #16, ahead of Lucas Auer’s Mercedes, Mike Rockenfeller’s Audi, Pascal Wehrlein, Augusto Farfus and Daniel Juncadella. Three bonus points for pole cut Paffett’s lead over di Resta to 26. Marco Wittmann could manage only 15th. Philipp Eng started his session with a trip through the gravel and qualified 18th, while Zanardi was 19th and last, 3.745s from pole and 0.940s behind Eng.

chapters.title: Drying track, mixed tyres and an early spin
text: The rain stopped before the start and the track began to dry, yet most of the field, including all six Audis, still chose wet tyres. Farfus and Bruno Spengler were among the few BMW drivers on slicks. Di Resta made a sluggish start from pole and was challenged by both Mortara and Paffett, but he held the outside line at the first corner and kept the lead.

The pit stops, which were mandatory, began early. Loïc Duval and Philipp Eng were first in, at the end of the third lap, with Eng’s BMW #25 climbing from 18th on the grid on a strategy that would define the race. Marco Wittmann’s BMW #11 was sent spinning by Robin Frijns on wet tyres and fell to the back before stopping for slicks. After six or seven laps di Resta and Paffett changed from wets to slicks together. Paffett rejoined narrowly ahead of Mortara, who had stopped earlier and was on warmer tyres, and held him off.

chapters.title: Paffett out, then chaos at the restart
text: A lap or so after his stop Paffett locked a wheel at Turn 8 and ran wide. As he came back onto the circuit, Mortara, defending from Eng, ran into him, damaging the steering, and the championship leader’s Mercedes #2 was out with the safety car deployed. Paffett said he had been on cold tyres while Mortara had warm ones. With Farfus and Juncadella, who had still not stopped, leading di Resta and Eng, the field restarted in two-by-two formation.

Farfus passed Juncadella, Eng gained places, and further back there was a pile-up. Rast and Jamie Green, in the second Rosberg Audi #53, collided, and Auer’s Mercedes #22 and Spengler’s BMW were also caught up. Joel Eriksson was given a drive-through penalty for contact with another car. Eng had a poor getaway at the next restart and dropped behind di Resta, but he regained the place when the Scot ran wide at Turn 8, and then took the lead. The Austrian, who had started 18th, built an advantage of around 2.6 seconds.

chapters.title: Frijns takes second on the last lap
text: With about ten minutes left Eng’s tyres began to go, and he said afterwards that contact during the race had forced him to push them harder. Di Resta and Mortara closed in and passed him around Turn 9, with the Scot taking the lead. Eng fell back to eighth, behind Glock. He said he had often pictured leading a DTM race and was disappointed it had not ended in victory.

Frijns, who started 12th, had been ninth after the second restart and fallen as low as 12th before he began to carve his way through the field. On the last lap he tried the inside of Mortara at Turn 8 and was beaten back. Mortara made a small mistake late on and Frijns went through, taking second place in the Abt Audi #4 and his first podium in the DTM. Juncadella’s Mercedes #23 had stopped with a failure five laps from the end, ending a drive in which he had led the race.

Di Resta won by 1.973 seconds from Frijns, with Mortara a further 0.171s behind. Duval was fourth, Nico Müller fifth and Wehrlein, up from eighth on the grid, sixth. Zanardi finished 13th in his first DTM race. It was di Resta’s third win of the season and it left Paffett only one point ahead in the championship, 177 to 176, with three Mercedes cars gone. “You don’t get better days,” the winner said.

facts.t: Nine in a row for Mercedes
facts.v: Di Resta’s 1m46.826s pole was Mercedes’ ninth consecutive DTM pole position, a longer run than any manufacturer had managed in the series.
